newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO mixed as US/Iraq tensions heighten.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO mixed as US/Iraq tensions heighten.

text.p: Traders were mixed over near-term market price direction of high sulphur fuel oil on Friday despite firm paper quotes and crude gains, as tensions in the Gulf heightened.
Firm crudes have caused September paper quotes to move higher to $115.50 per tonne from $114.50/$115.50 indicated on Thursday.

Chinese traders in Singapore said demand from China for October barrels were likely to increase. They said previous low imports for August and September barrels have drawn down domestic inventories. Chinese bids were heard between $120 and
Bunker demand was also firm, traders said. "The healthy demand will help support prices," a trader told Reuters.

But stocks in Singapore were high, traders said. Stocks figures released by the Trade Development Board (TDB) on Thursday showed a build of over one million barrels of fuel oil. Sellers continued to outnumber buyers in Singapore, traders said. There were at least four sellers still holding October barrels.
A Dutch trader said he would offer around current paper levels about $115 for October lifting 180-cst supplies.
The effect of crude gains on prices might be offset by healthy supplies, traders said.
